claims.summary: Under premise X of the Riesz mean formula from one premise (xi entire with the nontrivial zeros as its zeros and Re xi'/xi(s) = sum m_rho (sigma - beta)/|s - rho|^2) and the strip hypothesis, classical and imported, that every nontrivial zero has 0 < beta < 1. (1) For every real t the zeros with |gamma - t| <= 1 number at most 9 + (5/4) log(|t| + 2), with multiplicity. (2) If 1/2 <= theta <= 1 and every nontrivial zero has beta <= theta, then for tau >= 2 and tau <= y < y' <= 2y: |sum over y < n <= y' of Lambda(n) n^(-i tau)| <= C (y^theta log^2(tau + 2) + y tau^-1 log(2y)), C an absolute constant. (3) Hence for theta < 1 and y >= tau^(1/(1 - theta)) the sum is at most 8C y tau^-1 log^2 y; at theta = 1/2, the Riemann hypothesis, this is the premise of the sparse off-line exclusion with A = 2 for tau >= 2 and y >= tau^2.
claims.assessment: Conditional on premise X and the strip hypothesis, with a complete deduction: the count from the real part of xi'/xi at 2 + it and the series of the digamma function; the sum over a sharp interval compared with a trapezoid of ramps 1/tau, the edges bounded by Lambda(n) <= log n; the trapezoid as a second difference of the record's Riesz means, whose terms at a zero are bounded three ways and summed with the count. Classical in kind; not new. It shows that the conditional exclusion's premise follows from the goal from length tau^2 on; with a weaker bound on the zeros this argument gives it from a longer length, and that no shorter length is possible is not proved. The constant C is not computed. It gives no approach to the goal.
claims.rationale: Replaces an expectation the record leaned on, that the goal implies the premise of its one conditional exclusion for zeta, by a statement with a proof under one premise.
